questions.question: A user searches 'ERR-4012'. Which retrieval method is most likely to rank the right article first?
options: Dense vector search, because it understands meaning
Keyword search such as BM25, because the exact rare token matches
questions.explanation: Identifiers are exact strings; many embedders treat similar codes as nearly identical.

questions.question: What does IDF do in BM25?
options: Makes rare terms count much more than common ones
Limits how much repeated terms count
questions.explanation: ERR-4012 appears in one document, so matching it is strong evidence; 'account' appears in many.

questions.question: Why does reciprocal rank fusion use ranks instead of adding the two scores?
options: BM25 and cosine scores have different, unrelated scales, so adding them weights one side arbitrarily
It is required by vector databases
questions.explanation: 1/(k + rank) puts both rankings on the same footing.

questions.question: Why was 'rrf, zeros kept' worse than vector search alone?
options: Documents with BM25 score 0 still got ranks, and those arbitrary ranks voted in the fusion
questions.explanation: A zero-score document is not a weak match; it is not a match. Drop it before fusing.

questions.question: 'how do I get a refund' found nothing with BM25 although an article says 'refunds'. What is missing?
options: Stemming or normalising word forms, so refund and refunds count as the same term
questions.explanation: Without stemming, exact-term matching misses plural and other word forms.

questions.question: How should you show that hybrid search helps on your data?
options: Label queries by kind (identifiers vs paraphrases), and report each side and the fusion per kind
questions.explanation: Hybrid helps exactly when the two sides fail on different queries; per-kind results show whether they do.
